title: Need advice , frustrated with 3d model / animation
author: bebopbraunbaer
selftext:
I hope some has figured this out , cause I spend a lot of time and tokens without any payoff 

My pipeline looks like this :   
codex image generation with figure study , same figure , different angles , with helper lines and less then 5% variance 

this is going into blender to create the 3d model , and animations 

This is going into godot for meshes etc 

the only part I  satisfied with is the first step everything else looks .. miles from what I want 

I even tried dedicated services that create 3d models for you , no improvement 

I specifically selected a style with very simple geometry, nothing complicated about it so I think I am missing something crucial, do you see anything missing , or do you do it differently?

comments.author: ultra82
comments.body:
Let me share with you my experience, I tried ChatGPT image generation and various ways to generate some good animations, most of them failed miserably for me, but then I decided to try a specific technique (that actually I didn't know it has a name and I discovered it just after), look for a video (on Youtube for example) of a specific desired action, for example walking, running, kicking, etc. take the relevant part of the video, let's say 1-4 seconds of the actual action and ask Opus to cut the video frame by frame and run blender headlessly (it would also be token efficient doing it that way!) and replicate on a rigged model the position of the body parts frame by frame, with that technique you'll get more consistent results (at least that's how it worked for me). The more frames it will cut the more smoother and accurate result it will be.  
Turns out this technique has a name, and it's called roboscoping

Edit: I have to mention that I tested it only on a humanoid models, based on the images that you shared on other comments I guess you’re looking for a something a bit different. Well I hope my experience that I shared would be helpful anyhow.

replies.author: UndeniablyIffy
replies.body:
Exactly what I do, the cherry on top is telling Claude to assign a 'critique agent' which will fail all results if not within 9/10 accuracy to the reference. That's what brings the best results for me, however, it can take a LONG time if the animation or model is complex.  
  
I started using this workflow recently on my latest build and was using Opus High or Extra and was crushing usage. I made 11 models, most were OK, using Extra and I ran almost 50% of my usage down. I later tried a single model, similar in complexity as the others, and used opus medium and got comparable results with only 3% usage burn.
